title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Qualifications of Bidders in Judicial Auction of Real Property by People's Courts

articles.content_en: Article 1 Where a bidder who is subject to the purchase restriction policy of the locality where the property is located applies to participate in an auction of real property organized by a People's Court through judicial auction, the People's Court shall not permit such application.

Article 2 When a People's Court organizes an auction of real property through judicial auction, the auction notice published shall specify that a bidder must have the qualification to purchase a property and the corresponding legal consequences. Where a bidder applies to participate in the auction, it shall make an acceptance that it has the qualification to purchase a property and voluntarily bear the legal consequences.

Article 3 After a transaction is concluded in a judicial auction of real property, but before issuing a written ruling on transaction to the buyer, the People's Court shall review the evidentiary materials submitted by the buyer demonstrating that the buyer has met the qualification to purchase a property from the time of its application to participate in the auction to the time of issuing the written ruling on transaction. If, upon review, the buyer fails to meet the condition of continuously having the qualification to purchase a property, and the buyer requests the issuance of a written ruling on transaction by auction, the People's Court shall not permit such request.

Article 4 Where a buyer obtains the qualification to purchase a property by fraudulent means to participate in a judicial auction of real property and the auction is concluded, and the parties or interested persons claim that the auction act is void on the ground that it violates public order and good customs, the People's Court shall support such claim.
Where, pursuant to the preceding paragraph, the auction act is void due to the buyer's fraudulent obtainment of the qualification to purchase a property, the buyer shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 5 Where a judicial auction of real property results in a failed auction or other circumstances where it cannot be normally disposed of, and an applying enforcement party or other party who does not have the qualification to purchase a property requests to offset the debt with the property, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 6 Where, in a judicial auction of real property organized by a People's Court, a bidder obtains the qualification to purchase a property by fraudulent means, or parties collude maliciously, thereby infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of others or evading the performance of obligations determined by a legal instrument, the People's Court shall, according to the severity of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention. If a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 7 Except for the circumstances provided in the preceding six articles, other matters concerning the judicial auction of real property organized by a People's Court shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Online Judicial Auction by People's Courts, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Auction and Sale of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts, and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Article 8 Where a People's Court organizes a judicial sale of real property, these Provisions shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 9 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2022.
Where any judicial interpretation published by the Supreme People's Court before their coming into force is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
